utterances.text: Sir, Mr. ZM, in answering questions from my learned friend and the President of the Trial Chamber, you finally said that in these attacks of the 8th of June, units of the 3rd Corps took part -- actually, the 3rd Corps, and afterwards you remembered that the 1st Corps also took part, that is, a unit from Visoko. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BOHUTINSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: I would now like to ask you to look at paragraph 8 of your statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I suspect -- and I object to this course. It is not a proper procedure, with respect. I suspect that counsel is trying to indicate that there is something in the statement which may well be not the same thing as she wants to hear. And it is my submission that she ought to put the question directly to the witness first. It is his testimony in court which is evidence. If the witness answers one way, then it is permissible for them to use the statement to contradict him or for whatever purpose. But until the witness has answered the direct question, it is my submission that the statement ought not be put in front of him.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the witness has repeatedly answered this question, and I think that the purpose of the cross-examination is for me to check the credibility of the witness's answers. So I appeal to you to allow me to continue with my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We're going to withdraw for a couple of seconds to deliberate. It won't take long. We'll be back soon. --- Break taken at 1.31 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Regarding the question raised by the Defence, the Chamber notes that at the beginning the Prosecution, asking questions of the witness, obtained from the witness the identification of the units that prosecuted the attack by mentioning the 3rd Corps and the 7th Corps. After that, the Defence objected on a question when the witness, upon the request of the Chamber, indicated that there was a 3rd Corps and a unit from Visoko, which according to him belonged to the 1st Corps. The Defence, within the framework of the cross-examination asks the witness again whether during the attack the 3rd Corps was indeed present as well as a unit from Visoko. The witness confirmed that that was the answer he gave. At that point, the Prosecution wanted to show the witness a written statement where there was no mention of the unit from Visoko, and the Defence, to verify the credibility of the witness, wants to show him that sentence in the written statement signed by him. So the Chamber is of the opinion, when it comes to the credibility of the witness, it is possible for him to be asked to confirm a reply he gave in the examination-in-chief. The Defence, noting that that reply raises questions of credibility, wants to verify that answer by showing him the statement. So the Defence is allowed to ask the witness to read paragraph 8 of his statement and to tell us exactly what was meant by his statement, 3rd Corps, 7th Corps, 1st Corps. So please put the question to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Witness, please have a look at paragraph 8. Would it be correct to say that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Take your time. Read through paragraph 8 first. But read it to yourself. And then you will answer the Defence's question. Perhaps you have made a mistake. The purpose of the question is to establish the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Not an objection, but can I just quickly see what is being handed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The eighth paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He has read the eighth paragraph. Ask the witness your question now.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Mr. ZM, is it correct to say that in your statement given to the Prosecution you stated that you believed that units of the 3rd Corps and the 7th Corps of the ABiH participated in this offensive? And the 8th of June is referred to. Is that what you stated?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BOHUTINSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Is it correct to say that you then explained that the headquarters of the 7th Corps was in Travnik and its zone of responsibility extended from Ovnak to Travnik and the headquarters of the 3rd Corps was in Zenica and its zone of responsibility extended from Ovnak to Zenica? Is that what you said?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BOHUTINSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Did you also say, Mr. ZM -- is it correct to say that I'm quoting you -- did you say that the 7th Corps had a brigade comprised of refugees from Krajina and it was called the 7th Krajina Brigade?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BOHUTINSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: What you said is not in agreement with what you have testified about today before this Court; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BOHUTINSKI
utterances.text: Well, this is intelligence obtained. I can tell you that the 7th Corps was formed from the 3rd Corps, but I couldn't remember the date when the 7th Corps was established. But those units were formed from the 3rd Corps. The 7th Corps was formed from the 3rd Corps. All the units from the BH army that start with number 3 were part of the 3rd Corps. And that includes the 306th unit, et cetera, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Witness, everyone in the courtroom is trying to understand what you are saying, and to clarify what you are saying. It seems that some confusion has been created. It concerns the information that you obtained and the impression that you yourself had. So it's necessary to clarify this, and this is what the Defence is trying to do by putting questions to you. Can you make this clear for everyone. Can you make what you are saying clear for everyone. On the one hand, you mentioned information obtained from others; and on the other hand, you mentioned your personal knowledge. Can you clarify what the relation is between these two factors in order to make sure what the meaning of your answer to the Prosecution's questions was. So the Defence is trying to clarify your answers by asking you some questions. What everyone wants to know is which units participated in the operation. Either you should say that it's information that I obtained and I'm telling you that's the case. My testimony, what I said in paragraph 8, only reflects what I was informed of. Or otherwise, tell us that what is relevant is what you are testifying about here. Try to clarify this matter for us. If you are not in a position to do so, tell us that you can't.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, as I have said already, the 7th Corps was formed when the zone of responsibility of the 3rd Corps changed. I can't remember exactly when this happened, but the units in the area of Travnik municipality were an integral part of the 7th Corps or the battalion that was under the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you are telling us that in your opinion the units of the 3rd Corps had their name changed and they came to be called the 7th Corps; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The zone of responsibility of the 3rd Corps was reduced and the 7th Corps was established, but I can't remember the date when the 7th Corps was established. I don't know whether it was before the attack against us or after us. In any event, if the members of that unit who carried out the attack against our defence lines from the direction of Mehurici, Han Bila, if they weren't part of the 7th Corps, they were certainly part of the battalion subordinated to the 3rd Corps of the BH army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So does that mean that paragraph 8 that you have in front of you does not take into account this question in a very precise manner? In fact, the units of the 3rd Corps were placed under the control of the 7th Corps? Is that the case? This isn't what is stated in your written statement.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, it's not correct. The level of a corps -- a corps is under the Main Staff -- the main command of the BH army. But what I said about the brigade from Visoko, according to military rules any brigade that enters the zone of responsibility of a given corps, units of -- they're subordinated to that corps. So this brigade from Visoko - and I assume that it participated in the attacks - was subordinated to the 3rd Corps. It had to be subordinated to the 3rd Corps, according to the command structure. It had to be a part of the operative system and come under the orders of the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. May I continue?

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Would it be correct to say, Mr. ZM, that in paragraph 7 you said that from the direction of Zenica the 7th Muslim Brigade and the 327th Brigade took action?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BOHUTINSKI
utterances.text: This is information. The 314th and the 328th Brigade. There's a mistake here. It was the 328th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Would it be correct to say that in paragraph 12 at the end you said that from another direction the 328th Brigade also took part in the action? This is something that you also said in paragraph 11, in the last sentence of paragraph 11.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BOHUTINSKI
utterances.text: A brigade has it battalions.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: My question is whether I'm interpreting your statement correctly. In paragraph 11, you said that the 328th Brigade also took part in the action. You repeated this in the last sentence of paragraph 12. And in paragraph 7, you said that the 327th Brigade also participated in the action. Is that what it says?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BOHUTINSKI
utterances.text: In paragraph 7 it says that the 327th Brigade took part in the attack, but there is a mistake there. The brigade in question is the same; it's the 328th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Mr. ZM --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So we note that there is a mistake in the seventh paragraph. The number isn't "7." The number is "8." It's the 327th, not the 328th Brigade. That's what you wanted to show. Please carry on.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I'll tell the witness what I wanted to demonstrate.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Witness, you said -- well, let me put it this way: If I told you that the 7th Corps didn't exist in 1993, if I told you that it was formed in 1994, you would probably agree with me; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BOHUTINSKI
utterances.text: I said in the first statement that I gave I'm not sure. I said that I thought that it was formed in 1993 or in 1994.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: If I told you that in 1993, within the structure of the 3rd Corps there was a battalion or a division of no kind, these units didn't exist within the army structure, you would probably also agree with me; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BOHUTINSKI
utterances.text: Well, I wouldn't agree with you. I know for sure that the army command was in Travnik and at a higher level than the brigade level.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: If I told you, Mr. ZM, that within the army there was no brigade called the 328th Brigade, you would probably be able to agree with me.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BOHUTINSKI
utterances.text: I wouldn't agree with you if I didn't have reliable information about that beforehand.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: You would also agree with me that within the structure of the 3rd Corps of the BH army there was no 7th Krajina Brigade in existence.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BOHUTINSKI
utterances.text: I wouldn't agree with you.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: In fact, everything that you told the investigator at the time and everything you have testified about before the Court today is only the result of the fact that the intelligence you had was not sufficient and you personally never checked this intelligence; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BOHUTINSKI
utterances.text: Well, I wasn't in a position to verify this information.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: So in 1993, in fact you know nothing about the structure and the subordination system in the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BOHUTINSKI
utterances.text: I had some information, and I compiled a report on the basis of the information that I had.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: The information you had was obtained from civilians who would arrive in your area and certain intelligence officers from your battalion; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BOHUTINSKI
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: You never saw a single document which regulated the structure of the BH army or of the 3rd Corps in June 1993; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BOHUTINSKI
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. And the other Defence team? But I must tell them that time is flying.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. We only have two or three questions for this witness. But in view of the fact that the statement has already been shown to the witness, I would like it to be returned to the witness because I have some questions regarding paragraph 7 that Mrs. Residovic referred to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us proceed in the customary way. You first put the question to the witness, and then the paragraph will be shown to him. So put your question first, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. ZM, during your testimony today, you mentioned the units that took part in the offensive on the 8th of June, 1993; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BOHUTINSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Among others, you named the 7th Muslim Brigade.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BOHUTINSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness now be shown the statement that was shown to him a moment ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, in paragraph 7, you stated that the 7th Muslim Brigade was attacking in the area of Strmac; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BOHUTINSKI
utterances.text: Yes, according to intelligence reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: And that attack started at 8.00.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BOHUTINSKI
utterances.text: I think it started later.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: And it ended several hours after that.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BOHUTINSKI
utterances.text: I think it started in the afternoon, the attack on Strmac.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Strmac is an elevation above Susanj, Brajkovici; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BOHUTINSKI
utterances.text: No. It is an elevation above the village of Grahovcici.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have no further questions of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Does the Prosecution have any re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Just one or two questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You said -- you agreed with counsel who cross-examined you that you mentioned the 7th Corps in your statement, and your evidence is that the units that were involved in the attack belonged to the 3rd Corps. Now, in your explanation, you said that the 7th Corps was formed from the 3rd Corps. Were the units or some of the units involved in the attack of the 8th of June -- withdrawn. Withdrawn. Does that mean, does that statement that you made earlier mean that the units of the 7th -- some units of the 3rd Corps were later incorporated into the 7th Corps?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BOHUTINSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: But when you made your statement, you were not quite sure exactly when the 7th Corps was established.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BOHUTINSKI
utterances.text: I wasn't sure. I assumed it was 1993 or 1994. That is what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: So logically if the 7th Corps was established after the 8th of June, 1993, it follows that 7th Corps units could not have been involved in the attack.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The learned friend has answered the question --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the logic of the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. But the Prosecutor is not the witness, and he has answered his own logical question. So I don't think the witness should be allowed to answer that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I will respectfully say that it is essential that the witness, since he has the opportunity, to be allowed to make a comment on the logic, because it might explain the source of an error.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Stamp, put the question to him in a clear manner so that the witness can answer it clearly, but don't talk to him about a logic which is yours and which may not be his. So what is important is that he answer your question and not the logic that you feel that there is behind it. So ask him the question, and everyone is awaiting his answer with impatience.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Witness, the real question is, and the simple question is: What reason can you give to the Court for mentioning the 7th Brigade -- the 7th Corps in your statement? Because that is not consistent with your evidence today. How is it you came to say in your statement "the 7th Corps"? That is what I want to get to.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BOHUTINSKI
utterances.text: Because that corps had its command in Travnik and because the units from Travnik municipality and the broader area became part of that 7th Corps. Then it was formed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I understand that. Now, listen quite carefully to the question I'm asking. I'm asking you to explain to the Court what reasons there may be for saying in your statement that the 7th Corps was involved. That's all I'm asking. When today you say it was all the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The question is clear and it has the merit of being synthetic. Think over the question put to you. Think it over. Take your time before you answer it. The question is very clear.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You agreed --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Stamp, repeat the question in the same clear way.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I'll try, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You agreed that you said in your statement that the 7th Corps was involved. Today in your evidence you have said it was all the 3rd Corps was involved. Can you offer to us a reason why it is that you said "7th Corps" when you gave your statement? Is there a reason for this error?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BOHUTINSKI
utterances.text: Because the reports I had at the time were such that the 3rd Corps was formed prior to the offensive against our area, or rather, that the 7th Corps had been established. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Well, you just said something quite new. Was the 7th Corps established prior to or subsequent to the offensive of the 8th of June? Can you recall?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the witness answered that at the time he had operative information that the 7th Corps had already been formed, so I don't see what is unclear in the answer of the witness to this question.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: It is obviously unclear because it is not exactly what he said earlier. He had said something quite different at an earlier time. So he ought to be given an opportunity to clarify that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: It's a simple question, Witness. Can you recall when the 7th Brigade was formed? Was it formed before or after the 8th of June, 1993.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BOHUTINSKI
utterances.text: I told you a moment ago that I don't remember exactly when it was formed. But the intelligence information that we had at our disposal was --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: If you don't remember, you don't remember. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I have nothing further. May it please you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you. Witness, your testimony is over. We overran our time a little. But in view of the number of breaks, prompted either by the Prosecution or the Defence, we took a little more time, and we apologise to the interpreters for asking them to continue working more than normal. You have answered the questions of the Prosecution. You have answered the questions of the Defence, as well as questions from the Judges. We wish to thank you for the effort you made to remember developments in 1993, though this was a long time ago. Your testimony took place under conditions described at the beginning of the hearing. We wish you a safe journey home, hoping that you will be able to catch a plane shortly. And thank you once again for your testimony. I'm going to ask Madam Usher to lower the blinds so that the witness can leave this courtroom. Sir, you may now leave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I turn to Mr. Withopf now, for him to tell us the programme for next week.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. President. Good afternoon, counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. Withopf.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Good afternoon. Mr. President, Your Honours, as indicated in our recent confidential witness schedule, we will have three witnesses for next week. One witness will start on Monday; he will continue on Tuesday. There will be a second witness start on Tuesday, who will continue on Wednesday. And for Thursday and Friday, there will be another witness. As already indicated, in some instances the Prosecution will take longer for its examination-in-chief as in comparison to the Rule 65 ter summary. Defence has already -- has also informed the Prosecution that they may take substantially more time, as the Prosecution, for their cross-examination. Therefore, for the next week only three witnesses are scheduled. We will provide today, Mr. President, Your Honours, Defence counsel with a tentative schedule of all of our witnesses till the end of May in order to enable Defence a proper -- for a proper preparation of the cross-examination of such witnesses. However, I wish to emphasise it's a tentative schedule only.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Withopf. Has the Defence any remarks to make? No? In that case, I declare the hearing adjourned, and I invite the parties and the accused to come back for the hearing on Monday, which will begin at a quarter past 2.00. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 22nd day of March, 2004, at 2.15 p.m. 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 2.07 p.m.,
